chapter: Lee and Lester Young band remembered
title: Leo Watson of the Spirits of Rhythm
summary: Rowles describes Leo Watson's looks, drumming and wisecracks at the Capri.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Just before we forget. Leo Watson... You mentioned the Spirits of Rhythm Orchestra.
Not much is known about Leo except that he was a fantastic scat singer. But he must have been quite a talent.
Oh, Leo was too much. [Throw me that jacket, will you, Dan? Yeah, that one there.]
He was sumpin' else! Wild, crazy... He looked like he just came from a zoo and he spoke English. He had big, long

arms that would hung clear down below his knees, and he was bow-legged and flat-footed, and he was short, and his shoulders sloped, and he wore these zoot clothes. [CHUCKLES] His coat went way down below his knees. And he'd pick out these wild colors, like this, yellow or something... And his face was so black... And all he had to play on was a snare drum and a...
...a cymbal that he had on a stick, with a hole in the snare drum. [COUGHS]

And he had things he would do while we were playing, you know. Like, he'd do them in rhythm. Like, he'd holler out real loud, all of a sudden he'd holler out, "Carmen Miranda, how's your veranda?" or some crazy thing like that, you know.

I walked in there to work one night at the Capri, and they were up there playing... The Spirits always started. And I showed up for work, and I walked in, and there weren't too many people there, there were a few people... And I noticed this old man sitting, with a dark...black suit on, white-haired, just sitting there at the table, this little bar table -- you know how they had those little tables in these clubs. And he was just sitting there, just enthralled. He was back a ways; he wasn't up close -- about
twenty feet back, around the edge of the dance floor. And boy, that dance floor really saw some action. And you know who it was?

I became immediately very curious. I wanted to know who that guy was. Because Leo was just carrying on something terrible. He was like a spider monkey, prehensile tail and all. And he was just doing everything. Every time he saw me come in, no matter how many people were there, no matter what was going on, every time he saw me come in to come to work, he'd holler out... He'd be playin', you know, and he'd holler out...he'd stop and he'd stop and he'd say, "Jimmy Fiddler, how's your diddler?" -- and he'd sit down and start playing again! Oh...!! And I've got a picture somewhere, back in L.A., a smaller picture, a snapshot of Ben Webster on the bandstand, sitting in with us, and Leo is right beside him, playing and doing something, and Ben is just in hysterics -- he just can't play or nothing; he just can't do a thing, he's laughing so hard.
